name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*.*.*"]

permissions:
  contents: write
  id-token: write
  attestations: write

jobs:
  package:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
    env:
      NEXUS_BUILD_CONTAINER_IMAGE: rust:1.95.0-bookworm@sha256:4c2fd73ef19c5ef9d54bee03b06b2839a392604fbfcd578ed948b71b37c1d7fb
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - run: sudo apt-get update
      - run: sudo apt-get install --yes acl make bubblewrap build-essential meson ninja-build pkg-config libcap-dev
      - uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: '1.22.12'
      - name: Install pinned evaluator toolchains
        run: bash scripts/install-evaluator-toolchains.sh
      - run: bash scripts/ensure-ci-bubblewrap.sh
      - run: bash scripts/ensure-ci-user-cgroups.sh
      - name: Mount a dedicated capped tmpfs for evaluator resource fixtures
        run: |
          root=/mnt/nexus-eval-release
          sudo install -d -o "$USER" -g "$USER" -m 0711 "$root"
          sudo mount -t tmpfs -o size=128m,mode=0711,uid="$(id -u)",gid="$(id -g)" nexus-eval-release "$root"
          echo "NEXUS_EVAL_TEST_WORKSPACE_ROOT=$root" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          runtime_root=/opt/nexus-eval-ci-runtime
          sudo install -d -o "$USER" -g "$USER" -m 0711 "$runtime_root"
          echo "NEXUS_EVAL_TEST_RUNTIME_ROOT=$runtime_root" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@b725eda525362e7cf34af9a7243cac1e3f01a7ec # stable
      - name: Install cargo tools (audit, deny, about, cyclonedx)
        run: |
          CARGO_HOME="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}"
          export CARGO_HOME
          mkdir -p "$CARGO_HOME/bin"
          echo "$CARGO_HOME/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$CARGO_HOME/bin:$PATH"
          cargo install cargo-audit --locked --version 0.22.2
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny/releases/download/0.20.2/cargo-deny-0.20.2-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz | tar -xz -C "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          mv "$RUNNER_TEMP/cargo-deny-0.20.2-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/cargo-deny" "$CARGO_HOME/bin/"
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/EmbarkStudios/cargo-about/releases/download/0.9.2/cargo-about-0.9.2-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz | tar -xz -C "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          mv "$RUNNER_TEMP/cargo-about-0.9.2-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/cargo-about" "$CARGO_HOME/bin/"
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/CycloneDX/cyclonedx-rust-cargo/releases/download/cargo-cyclonedx-0.5.9/cargo-cyclonedx-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.xz | tar -xJ -C "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          mv "$RUNNER_TEMP/cargo-cyclonedx-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/cargo-cyclonedx" "$CARGO_HOME/bin/"
          curl -fsSL https://github.com/CycloneDX/cyclonedx-cli/releases/download/v0.33.1/cyclonedx-linux-x64 -o "$CARGO_HOME/bin/cyclonedx"
          chmod +x "$CARGO_HOME/bin/cyclonedx"
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 22.22.1
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: cli/package-lock.json
      - name: Require the pinned release Node and npm versions
        run: |
          test "$(node --version)" = "v22.22.1"
          test "$(npm --version)" = "10.9.4"
      - name: Install selected Node runtime for isolated evaluation commands
        run: |
          node_runtime="$(readlink -f "$(command -v node)")"
          npm_cli="$(readlink -f "$(command -v npm)")"
          npm_root="$(dirname "$(dirname "$npm_cli")")"
          case "$npm_root" in */lib/node_modules/npm) ;; *) echo "Unexpected setup-node npm package path" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
          test -f "$npm_root/package.json"
          sudo install -o root -g root -m 0755 "$node_runtime" /usr/bin/node
          sudo install -d -o root -g root -m 0755 /usr/lib/nexus-ci/npm
          sudo cp -a "$npm_root/." /usr/lib/nexus-ci/npm/
          sudo chown -hR root:root /usr/lib/nexus-ci/npm
          sudo chmod 0755 /usr/lib/nexus-ci/npm/bin/npm-cli.js
          sudo ln -sfn /usr/lib/nexus-ci/npm/bin/npm-cli.js /usr/bin/npm
          test "$(/usr/bin/node --version)" = "$(node --version)"
          test "$(env PATH=/usr/bin:/bin /usr/bin/npm --version)" = "$(npm --version)"
      - name: Require a version-matched tag on main
        run: |
          git fetch origin main --no-tags
          git merge-base --is-ancestor "$GITHUB_SHA" origin/main
          test "${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}" = "$(node -p 'require("./package.json").version')"
          node scripts/sync-version.mjs --check --tag "$GITHUB_REF_NAME"
          test -f "docs/releases/${GITHUB_REF_NAME}.md" || { echo "Missing docs/releases/${GITHUB_REF_NAME}.md" >&2; exit 1; }
      - name: Require a stable tag to be a version-only commit on its RC
        if: ${{ !contains(github.ref_name, '-') }}
        # The checkout has full history and tags (fetch-depth: 0). The checker runs from the RC's own copy so a stable
        # commit cannot replace it; branch and tag protection remain the control over the workflow file itself.
        run: |
          rc="$(git tag --points-at "$GITHUB_SHA^" | grep -E "^${GITHUB_REF_NAME//./\\.}-rc\.[0-9]+$" | sort -V | tail -n 1 || true)"
          test -n "$rc" || { echo "the parent of $GITHUB_REF_NAME is not a ${GITHUB_REF_NAME}-rc.N tag" >&2; exit 1; }
          git show "$rc:scripts/check-version-only-diff.mjs" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/check-version-only-diff.mjs"
          node "$RUNNER_TEMP/check-version-only-diff.mjs" "$rc" "$GITHUB_SHA"
      - run: npm ci --prefix cli
      - run: npm --prefix cli run build
      - run: cargo test --locked --manifest-path core/Cargo.toml
      - run: cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path core/Cargo.toml --bin harness-core --bin nexus-tui
      - name: Run the CLI suite with a hang bound
        # Normal runs take 12-20 minutes; a test process that never exits must fail the job, not hold it for 6 hours.
        timeout-minutes: 45
        run: npm --prefix cli test
      - run: bash scripts/security_gates.sh
      - run: bash scripts/package-linux.sh "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist"
      - run: bash scripts/package-linux.sh "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" "$RUNNER_TEMP/repro-check"
      - run: cmp "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist/nexus-linux-x86_64-$GITHUB_REF_NAME.tar.gz" "$RUNNER_TEMP/repro-check/nexus-linux-x86_64-$GITHUB_REF_NAME.tar.gz"
      - run: cmp "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist/SHA256SUMS" "$RUNNER_TEMP/repro-check/SHA256SUMS"
      - run: cmp "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt" "$RUNNER_TEMP/repro-check/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt"
      - run: cyclonedx validate --input-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist/sbom.cdx.json" --fail-on-errors
      - run: cmp "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist/sbom.cdx.json" "$RUNNER_TEMP/repro-check/sbom.cdx.json"
      - run: cmp "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist/install.sh" "$RUNNER_TEMP/repro-check/install.sh"
      - run: bash scripts/smoke-package.sh "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist/nexus-linux-x86_64-$GITHUB_REF_NAME.tar.gz"
      - run: bash scripts/installer-smoke.sh "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/install.sh" "$RUNNER_TEMP/dist/nexus-linux-x86_64-$GITHUB_REF_NAME.tar.gz"
      - name: Attest build provenance
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/dist/nexus-linux-x86_64-${{ github.ref_name }}.tar.gz
            ${{ runner.temp }}/dist/SHA256SUMS
      # RC tags (vX.Y.Z-rc.N) publish a prerelease: the workflow-produced RC is the qualification candidate
      # (ACCEPTANCE §1.1 stage 2). Stable tags only build an unpublished draft (stage 5); it is published by hand with
      # `gh release edit <tag> --draft=false` after the stable artifact checks and the signed acceptance disposition.
      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@8a0cd651e5b2365bd640854a3fa5dfc70e4875f3 # v3.0.4
        with:
          files: ${{ runner.temp }}/dist/*
          body_path: docs/releases/${{ github.ref_name }}.md
          prerelease: ${{ contains(github.ref_name, '-') }}
          draft: ${{ !contains(github.ref_name, '-') }}

# Nexus Code

[![GitHub Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/mikeholownych/nexus-code?include_prereleases&style=flat-square&color=blue)](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/releases)
[![CI Status](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/mikeholownych/nexus-code/ci.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=CI)](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/actions)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT%20%7C%20Apache--2.0-yellow.svg?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)
[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-Linux%20x86__64-orange?style=flat-square)](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#release-package)
[![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-%E2%89%A522-brightgreen?style=flat-square)](https://nodejs.org/)
[![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-2024%20%7C%201.85%2B-red?style=flat-square)](https://www.rust-lang.org/)

**Nexus Code** is an open-source, local-first AI coding agent and execution harness. It pairs a TypeScript agent and sidecar with native Rust workspace tools and a Ratatui terminal user interface (TUI), with opt-in sandboxing, human approval modes, and Git worktree isolation.

> **Status:** the latest stable release is [v1.1.3](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/releases). v1.1.4 is in development: its work ledger is closed and qualification is pending. Development plans and this README do not establish release readiness; see [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/releases) and [`docs/releases/`](docs/releases/).
>
> The Cloudflare contest entry is historical: see [docs/CLOUDFLARE_CONTEST.md](docs/CLOUDFLARE_CONTEST.md).

---

## Table of Contents

- [Why Nexus Code?](#why-nexus-code)
- [Architecture Overview](#architecture-overview)
- [Quick Start](#quick-start)
  - [Installation](#1-installation)
  - [Inference Setup](#2-inference-setup)
  - [First Run](#3-first-run)
- [Execution Modes & Workflows](#execution-modes--workflows)
  - [Interactive TUI](#interactive-terminal-ui)
  - [Command-Line REPL](#command-line-repl)
  - [Autonomous Non-Interactive Run](#autonomous-task-execution)
- [Core Capabilities](#core-capabilities)
  - [Security & Sandboxing](#defense-in-depth-sandboxing)
  - [Git Worktree Isolation](#git-worktree-isolation)
  - [Human-in-the-Loop Controls](#human-in-the-loop-hitl-approvals)
  - [Context Budgeting & Cost Governance](#context-budgeting--cost-governance)
  - [Universal Model Ecosystem & MCP](#universal-model-support--mcp)
- [Common Commands & Slash Actions](#common-commands--slash-actions)
- [Building from Source](#building-from-source)
- [Repository Structure](#repository-structure)
- [Documentation Index](#documentation-index)
- [Contributing & Community](#contributing--community)
- [License](#license)

---

## Why Nexus Code?

Nexus Code's design choices:

- **Approval by Default:** Unset permission mode is `review`: file writes, shell commands, and network egress need your confirmation. File tools are confined to the workspace, and `--sandbox` adds Linux Bubblewrap (`bwrap`) or Docker isolation for commands (see the [architecture reference](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for limits).
- **Opt-in Git Worktree Isolation:** Pass `--worktree` (ephemeral) or `--worktree-branch <name>` (named, kept) and the run happens in a lightweight Git worktree under `.nexus/worktrees/` instead of your active checkout; without either flag it runs in your checkout. See [docs/WORKTREES.md](docs/WORKTREES.md).
- **Terminal UI:** Built on [Ratatui](https://ratatui.rs/), the live interface streams tokens, takes keyboard approvals, and offers diff review.
- **Verification before merge:** `nexus worktree merge` requires a recorded passing verification for the exact state being merged, unless you pass `--no-verify-receipt --reason`.
- **Cost & Context Protection:** Token tracking, context compaction, and optional cloud limits (`NEXUS_CLOUD_MAX_COST_USD`; only enforceable when the provider reports cost).

---

## Architecture Overview

Nexus Code uses a hybrid, decoupled architecture:
1. **Front-End & Terminal Experience (`core/src/bin/nexus_tui`):** Rust binary using Ratatui and crossterm for diff rendering, event handling, and terminal management.
2. **Agent Brain & Sidecar (`cli/`):** TypeScript-driven execution loop handling turn dispatch, LLM conversation state, tool calling, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and context compaction.
3. **Workspace Tools Engine (`core/src/` / `harness-core`):** Rust tools implementing file operations, unified diff generation, symbol parsing, and command execution.

```mermaid
graph TD
    User([Developer / Terminal]) <-->|Keystrokes / ANSI Output| TUI[nexus-tui\nRatatui / Rust]
    TUI <-->|NDJSON over stdio| Sidecar[Agent Sidecar\nTypeScript / Node.js 22+]
    
    subgraph Agent Runtime
        Sidecar --> Context[Context Budgeting & Compaction]
        Sidecar --> Approval[Approval Policy & Egress Guard]
        Sidecar --> Models[Local & Cloud LLMs\nvLLM / Ollama / Anthropic / OpenAI]
        Sidecar --> MCP[Model Context Protocol Hub]
    end

    Sidecar <-->|CLI / NDJSON| CoreTools[harness-core\nRust Native Engine]

    subgraph Workspace ["Workspace (opt-in sandbox / worktree)"]
        CoreTools --> Disk[(Project Workspace)]
        CoreTools -.->|--sandbox| Sandbox[Linux bwrap / Docker]
        Sandbox -.-> Disk
        Worktrees[Optional git worktree\n.nexus/worktrees/branch] -.-> Disk
    end
```

---

## Quick Start

### 1. Installation

On Linux x86-64 (glibc 2.35+ and Node.js 22+):

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/main/install.sh | sh
```

The installer verifies SHA-256 checksums, installs the client package into `~/.local/lib/nexus`, and creates a symlink at `~/.local/bin/nexus`. Ensure `~/.local/bin` is in your `PATH`:

```sh
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```

> [!NOTE]
> To pin a release or install a prerelease, set `NEXUS_VERSION` to a tag from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/releases):
> ```sh
> curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mikeholownych/nexus-code/main/install.sh | NEXUS_VERSION=v1.1.3 sh
> ```

### 2. Inference Setup

Nexus Code connects to any OpenAI-compatible local server (e.g. Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM, LM Studio) or cloud provider.

Configure your endpoint in `~/.config/nexus/config.env`:

```sh
mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/nexus"
chmod 700 "$HOME/.config/nexus"
cat > "$HOME/.config/nexus/config.env" <<'EOF'
LOCAL_LLM_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:1234/v1
LOCAL_LLM_MODEL=qwen2.5-coder-7b-instruct
LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY=REDACTED
EOF
chmod 600 "$HOME/.config/nexus/config.env"
```

For cloud providers (Anthropic Claude or OpenAI), see [Cloud Providers Guide](docs/CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md).

### 3. First Run

Navigate to any git repository and start Nexus Code:

```sh
cd /path/to/your/project
nexus
```

---

## Execution Modes & Workflows

### Interactive Terminal UI
Running `nexus` in a standard terminal launches the full-screen interactive TUI:
```sh
nexus
```
- Real-time token streaming and syntax highlighting.
- Visual approval prompt for shell execution and file modification.
- Multi-line composer and bracketed paste handling.
- Use `/help` for available slash commands, `/model` to switch providers, or `Esc` to cancel the active turn.

### Command-Line REPL
For terminal multiplexers, remote SSH sessions, or plain terminal workflows:
```sh
nexus repl
```
Provides the full conversational agent with line-based interactive approval prompts.

### Autonomous Task Execution
Execute a targeted objective without the interactive UI and exit when the run finishes:
```sh
nexus run "Add unit tests for the token bucket rate limiter in src/rate_limiter.ts"
```
Approval prompts still apply unless you choose `--mode auto` or `--yes`; see the [User Manual](docs/USER_MANUAL.md). Add `--worktree-branch <name>` to run inside a named worktree that is kept after the run.

---

## Core Capabilities

### Defense-in-Depth Sandboxing
- **Workspace path jail:** the Rust file tools reject paths outside the workspace, including `..` and symlink escapes.
- **Opt-in command sandbox:** `--sandbox` runs commands under Bubblewrap (`bwrap`) or Docker. Without it, host commands have your filesystem access; `--read-only` masks `$HOME` when `bwrap` is available.
- **Egress approval:** network access asks on first use of each origin, except under `--yes`.

[`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) lists each guarantee and its limits.

### Git Worktree Isolation
Eliminate uncommitted workspace pollution with native named worktrees (see [docs/WORKTREES.md](docs/WORKTREES.md)):
- Run speculative features under `.nexus/worktrees/<branch>` (or configured sibling directories) without touching your checked-out files.
- `nexus worktree switch -c <branch>` (or session `/worktree switch -c <branch>`) creates an isolated branch checkout; `nexus run --worktree-branch <branch> "<task>"` runs a task inside one.
- `nexus worktree merge` squashes, rebases, and fast-forwards the branch into the default branch, then removes the worktree. It needs a recorded passing verification (or `--no-verify-receipt --reason`); `--ai-message` drafts the commit message with your configured model.
- `nexus worktree prune` removes worktrees already integrated into the default branch (`--dry-run` first), `nexus worktree remove <branch>` removes one, and `nexus worktree list --json` inspects them.

### Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Approvals
Stay in complete control of changes:
- **`review` mode (default):** Prompts for confirmation before file writes, shell commands, or network calls. `--yes` bypasses all prompts.
- **`auto` mode (`--mode auto`):** Writes and commands run without approval; network egress still asks on first use of each origin.
- **`read-only` mode (`--read-only`):** Explores code without permitting modifications or non-read commands.

### Context Budgeting & Cost Governance
- Tracks token use against the model's context limit.
- Compacts older conversation turns when context headroom shrinks.
- Optional cloud ceilings via `NEXUS_CLOUD_MAX_REQUESTS`, `NEXUS_CLOUD_MAX_TOKENS` and `NEXUS_CLOUD_MAX_COST_USD`.

### Universal Model Support & MCP
- Local inference: native support for llama.cpp, Ollama, and vLLM (see [docs/LOCAL_SERVERS.md](docs/LOCAL_SERVERS.md)).
- Cloud provider support with secret redaction and configurable cost governance (see [docs/CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md](docs/CLOUD_PROVIDERS.md)).
- MCP client: connect external MCP servers (`.mcp.json` or `~/.config/nexus/mcp.json`) to expose their tools; see [docs/MCP_GUIDE.md](docs/MCP_GUIDE.md).

## 3. High-Efficiency Tooling Parity
## 3. High-Efficiency Tooling Parity

Nexus Code provides high-performance tools executed via compiled native 64-bit Rust ELF, persistent JSON-RPC stdio daemon, and async Tokio runtime:

1. **`read_file`**: Read file lines with line numbering and range slices using zero-copy `memmap2`.
2. **`batch_read`**: Read multiple files in parallel in a single turn.
3. **`file_tree`**: Render directory tree hierarchy respecting `.gitignore`.
4. **`file_info`**: Inspect file size, permissions, line count, binary status, and modified timestamps.
5. **`edit_file`**: Exact search-and-replace of a snippet that must occur once (or every occurrence with `replace_all`). Blank lines around the snippet are tolerated; a snippet that matches only with different indentation is refused with the file's exact lines quoted. CRLF files keep CRLF.
6. **`patch_file`**: Apply standard unified diffs and patch hunks.
7. **`search_code`**: Multi-threaded ripgrep code search across workspace.
8. **`trigram_search`**: Ultra-fast code search accelerated by Rust inverted trigram index.
9. **`search_symbols`**: AST-level symbol search for function, struct, interface declarations.
10. **`cst_symbols`**: Concrete Syntax Tree parser extracting multiline signatures, doc comments, visibility, and scopes.
11. **`git_status`**: Native repository status (branch, clean/dirty, staged, modified, untracked) via `git2`.
12. **`git_diff`**: Native unified diff generation via `git2`.
13. **`git_log`**: Native commit history retrieval via `git2`.
14. **`run_command`**: Execute commands with non-blocking pipes, safety guards, and PTY pseudo-terminal support.
15. **`run_tests`**: Auto-detect and run project test suites with structured failure parsing and compiler diagnostics.
16. **`lsp_hover`**: Query Language Server Protocol hover documentation and type signatures.
17. **`lsp_definition`**: Query LSP symbol definition locations.
18. **`lsp_diagnostics`**: Query LSP compiler diagnostics and inline errors.
19. **`search_web`**: Technical web search engine for API documentation and solutions.
20. **`update_plan`**: Maintain multi-phase milestone tracking.
21. **`spawn_subagent`**: Delegate subtasks to isolated sub-agents.
22. **`activate_skill`**: Load specialized agent knowledge into context dynamically.
23. **`fetch_web`**: Outbound HTTP scraper with SSRF protection and allowed domain filtering.
24. **`task_completed`**: Finalize turn with comprehensive report.

With no clipboard tool (`wl-copy`, `xclip`, `xsel`, `pbcopy`: SSH, tmux, headless) the live TUI asks the terminal to copy it with an OSC 52 request instead (up to 74,994 bytes; larger text is refused, never cut). The terminal does not confirm it: terminals may ignore OSC 52, tmux needs `set -g set-clipboard on`, GNU screen is not supported. The text reaches the terminal only base64-encoded, after the same credential redaction and control-character handling as every sidecar message. `NEXUS_OSC52=off` (also `0`, `false`, `no`, `none`) turns the fallback off, and the older line-mode REPL does not use it. |

## 3. High-Efficiency Tooling Parity
## 3. High-Efficiency Tooling Parity

Nexus Code provides high-performance tools executed via compiled native 64-bit Rust ELF, persistent JSON-RPC stdio daemon, and async Tokio runtime:

1. **`read_file`**: Read file lines with line numbering and range slices using zero-copy `memmap2`.
2. **`batch_read`**: Read multiple files in parallel in a single turn.
3. **`file_tree`**: Render directory tree hierarchy respecting `.gitignore`.
4. **`file_info`**: Inspect file size, permissions, line count, binary status, and modified timestamps.
5. **`edit_file`**: Exact search-and-replace of a snippet that must occur once (or every occurrence with `replace_all`). Blank lines around the snippet are tolerated; a snippet that matches only with different indentation is refused with the file's exact lines quoted. CRLF files keep CRLF.
6. **`patch_file`**: Apply standard unified diffs and patch hunks.
7. **`search_code`**: Multi-threaded ripgrep code search across workspace.
8. **`trigram_search`**: Ultra-fast code search accelerated by Rust inverted trigram index.
9. **`search_symbols`**: AST-level symbol search for function, struct, interface declarations.
10. **`cst_symbols`**: Concrete Syntax Tree parser extracting multiline signatures, doc comments, visibility, and scopes.
11. **`git_status`**: Native repository status (branch, clean/dirty, staged, modified, untracked) via `git2`.
12. **`git_diff`**: Native unified diff generation via `git2`.
13. **`git_log`**: Native commit history retrieval via `git2`.
14. **`run_command`**: Execute commands with non-blocking pipes, safety guards, and PTY pseudo-terminal support.
15. **`run_tests`**: Auto-detect and run project test suites with structured failure parsing and compiler diagnostics.
16. **`lsp_hover`**: Query Language Server Protocol hover documentation and type signatures.
17. **`lsp_definition`**: Query LSP symbol definition locations.
18. **`lsp_diagnostics`**: Query LSP compiler diagnostics and inline errors.
19. **`search_web`**: Technical web search engine for API documentation and solutions.
20. **`update_plan`**: Maintain multi-phase milestone tracking.
21. **`spawn_subagent`**: Delegate subtasks to isolated sub-agents.
22. **`activate_skill`**: Load specialized agent knowledge into context dynamically.
23. **`fetch_web`**: Outbound HTTP scraper with SSRF protection and allowed domain filtering.
24. **`task_completed`**: Finalize turn with comprehensive report.

# Evaluation harness (qualification assessment §9)

`run.mjs` runs tasks against one agent configuration and appends a JSON line per run; `score.mjs` reports the scores
separately (never combined), per task and configuration, with 95 % Wilson intervals.

`docs/v1.0.0/READINESS.md` is a historical checkpoint at source revision `6151a23`; use this file and the current
runner source for evaluator behavior added after that revision. Neither document represents completed M5 qualification.

```bash
node eval/run.mjs --config eval/configs/gateway-engineering-deep.json --out eval/out/<label> [--only id,id] [--runs N]
node eval/score.mjs eval/out/<label>/results.jsonl          # markdown table; --json for machine output
node eval/score.mjs --pairs "$NEXUS_RESULTS" "$GOOSE_RESULTS" "$OPENCODE_RESULTS"
```

## Installed versioned datasets

Installed releases expose the versioned runner through the Nexus CLI:

```bash
nexus eval --dataset /path/to/core-v1 --split benchmark --runs 1 \
  --isolated-home --output ./results/benchmark.json
```

The dataset path must be a versioned dataset directory. The installed command loads its runner from the package named by
`NEXUS_HOME`; it does not fall back to evaluator code in a development checkout. The score file is created with
owner-only permissions, and per-task run artifacts are written beside it under `<output>.artifacts`. The legacy
`nexus eval <dataset-file> --limit N` form remains available for file-based benchmark datasets. `--limit` is not
supported for versioned dataset directories; select `--split` or provide a dataset containing the desired task set.

Each run uses a frozen copy of the task tree, a fresh workspace and `HOME`, and a unique output directory. The agent
receives only its workspace, isolated home, selected read-only runtime files, and a run-scoped token for a local proxy;
the real gateway credential stays in the harness process. The candidate runs in Bubblewrap user, PID and network
namespaces, with nested user namespaces disabled. Legacy development tasks may still use `hidden: { dir, into, command }`;
those commands execute against the candidate workspace after the agent exits and are **not safe for qualification**, because
validator code can inspect or modify files in that workspace. Qualification requires `hidden: { protocol: "blackbox-v1",
casesFile, runtime, argv, timeoutMs, totalTimeoutMs, maxOutputBytes }`. Its private JSON cases contain only `input` and
`expected`; the host evaluator keeps expected values in its process and launches the candidate runtime separately for each
input using a fresh top-level Bubblewrap boundary. The candidate receives one input on stdin and returns one JSON value on
stdout. Its workspace is read-only; private oracle files are not mounted. Candidate output and diagnostics are discarded,
and result logs contain only case counts and failed indexes. Supported runtimes are explicitly allowlisted (`node`,
`python3`); the only argument is a validated relative candidate entrypoint (no runtime flags, eval expressions, or extra
arguments), and per-case/aggregate time and output bounds are enforced. Oracle files must be outside the copied fixture.
Absolute paths, traversal, symlinks and unsupported fixture entries are rejected. `manifest.json` records the harness source-file hashes, model fingerprint, corpus/task
hashes when qualification is configured, executable version, budgets, host and Node version. Each result records the
executable version and effective step/minute budget; per-run logs go to `logs/<task>-<run>/`. The runner refuses an
existing output directory so a retry cannot append to or replace prior evidence.

Qualification runs require `nexusExecutable` to name the absolute path of the installed RC,
`expectedAgentVersion` to pin its version, and `nexusPackageSha256` to record the expected release-asset digest from checksum verification. The runner checks `nexus --version` and refuses the checkout
`cli/dist/index.js` or a version mismatch before starting an agent. Peer versions are read using each adapter's

# Peer coding-harness reference (documented capabilities only)

Researched 2026-10-12 from primary sources (official docs, official repos/releases, vendor posts). Every fact below is
**documented** by the vendor/project; nothing here is measured. Citation keys are in brackets; the citation list gives
URL and the version/date seen. Benchmark figures are **vendor claims about models, not harness measurements**, and are
not parity evidence for Nexus.

Peers: OpenAI **Codex CLI** (stable 0.162.1), Anthropic **Claude Code** (2.1.296), **OpenCode** (v1.19.0, anomalyco/opencode),
**Goose** (v1.54.0, AAIF/Linux Foundation), **Aider** (0.86.2). OpenCode, Goose and Aider were chosen because they
document local-model support (Ollama / LM Studio / OpenAI-compatible) and a terminal interface.

## 1. Comparison table

| Area | Codex CLI | Claude Code | OpenCode | Goose | Aider |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| **2. Context / long tasks** | `/compact`; `model_auto_compact_token_limit`, `model_context_window`; `/status` shows context usage; `codex resume`; `/fork` copies a chat to a new chat or worktree; `tool_output_token_limit`; resumable state in a SQLi
| **3. Tools / execution** | Shell tool on by default; background terminals (`background_terminal_max_timeout` 300000 ms); MCP `tool_timeout_sec` 60, `startup_timeout_sec` 10; subagents; managed git worktree tools (0.162.0); `/worktree` [CX-CFG][CX-R
| **4. Operator control / trust** | Sandbox modes `read-only` / `workspace-write` / `danger-full-access`; macOS Seatbelt, Linux bubblewrap (PATH or bundled helper needing unprivileged userns), WSL2 Linux sandbox, native Windows sandbox; `writable_roo
| **5. Inference compatibility** | Built-in providers `openai`, `ollama`, `lmstudio`; `--oss` with `oss_provider = lmstudio|ollama`; custom `model_providers.<id>.base_url`; `wire_api` only `responses` (Responses API required); `request_max_retries` 4
| **6. Terminal experience** | Live commands/diffs, syntax theme (`tui.theme`), remappable keymap incl. `approval` context, vim mode, status line, notifications (OSC9/BEL), alternate-screen control, raw output toggle; `file_opener` for IDE links; IDE
| **7. Persistence / audit** | `history.jsonl` (`history.persistence save-all|none`, `max_bytes`); `log_dir`; SQLite runtime state; OTel logs/traces/metrics exporters (`otlp-http`/`otlp-grpc`), metrics default `statsig`, raw prompt export opt-in (`ot
| **8. Product delivery** | Install script (`releases.openai.com`, GitHub fallback), npm, Homebrew cask, GitHub binaries; macOS arm64/x86_64, Linux x86_64/arm64 (musl), Windows; Apache-2.0; signed PowerShell installer (0.162.0); near-daily releases (
| **9. Evaluation (vendor claims)** | OpenAI claims for **models** (not the CLI harness): GPT-5.5 82.7% Terminal-Bench 2.0, 58.6% SWE-Bench Pro [EV-OAI]. | Anthropic claims for **models**: Claude Opus 4.6 65.4% Terminal-Bench 2.0 (max effort), 80.8% 

## 2. Evaluation suites (for a matched Nexus evaluation)

- **SWE-bench / SWE-bench Verified** [EV-SWE][EV-SWEDOC]: given a real GitHub repository and issue, the system must produce
  a patch that resolves it; graded by the project's tests in a Docker-based harness. Verified = "500 engineer-confirmed
  solvable problems" (released 2024-08-13). Leaderboard variants: Verified, Lite, Full, Multilingual, Multimodal, plus a
  "Bash Only" filter (mini-SWE-agent). Measures patch correctness on Python repo issues; does not measure UX, approvals or
  long-session behaviour.
- **Terminal-Bench** [EV-TB][EV-TBGH][EV-TBDOC]: each task = English instruction + test script that verifies completion +
  reference ("oracle") solution, executed in an isolated terminal sandbox; measures end-to-end terminal work ("compiling
  code to training models and setting up servers"). Original beta ~100 tasks (`tb` CLI); 2.0+ run via the Harbor framework;
  tbench.ai currently shows version 4.0 with a leaderboard of model+agent pairs (resolution rate, cost, tokens, 95% CIs);
  example run: `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`, `-e modal`, agent `claude-code`, `-k 5`. Some tasks need GPUs.
- Matched-evaluation implication: Terminal-Bench (via Harbor) evaluates **agent+model pairs**, so Nexus, Codex CLI,
  OpenCode and Goose can be compared with the *same local model* and same task set; SWE-bench Verified compares patch
  outcomes. Vendor model scores above use different harnesses/models and cannot stand in for such a run.

## 3. Behavioural reference points for Nexus (testable)

Each line is a behaviour at least one peer documents; phrased so a test can pass/fail it. Source keys in brackets.

Objective completion
1. An operator can enter a read-only plan mode in which file edits are blocked until the operator approves a plan [CC-PERM][OC-AGENTS][CX-SLASH].
2. An operator can set a persistent goal with explicit completion/verification criteria; the agent keeps working across turns until those criteria are checked, and the goal survives resume [CX-LONG][CC-SESS].
3. With a configured test command, the harness runs it after edits and feeds non-zero-exit output back for a fix attempt [AI-LINT].
4. A visible task list is maintained and updated as steps complete [CC-TOOLS].
5. A hard cap on consecutive autonomous actions exists; on reaching it the harness asks rather than silently stopping [GS-CTX].
6. Identical repeated tool calls (e.g. 3x same input) are detected and escalated to the operator [OC-PERM].

Context / long tasks
7. Automatic compaction triggers before the context window is exceeded, with a configurable threshold, and a manual `/compact [focus]` exists [CC-CTX][GS-CTX][OC-CFG][CX-CFG].
8. After compaction, project instructions (AGENTS.md-equivalent) and recently edited files are re-injected [CC-CTX].
9. Context usage is visible on demand (status/context command or indicator) [CX-SLASH][CC-SESS][GS-CTX].
10. With a local backend whose server-side context is smaller than the request, the harness does not silently lose context (sets/validates `num_ctx`/context length or warns) [AI-OLLAMA][GS-PROV].
11. Sessions resume after exit, and can be forked/branched leaving the original intact [CC-SESS][CX-SLASH].
12. On resume after a crash, a tool call that was in flight is marked interrupted and is not blindly re-executed [CC-SESS].
58:1. **Workspace path jail (file tools).** The Rust file tools (read, write, edit, delete, list, search) canonicalize every path against the workspace root and reject `..`, absolute paths and symlink escapes, rechecking the opened descriptor. *Limit:* for `run_command`, path protection is advisory. Host commands have the user's filesystem access unless the sandbox (`--sandbox`) or read-only HOME masking (`--read-only` with `bwrap`) is enabled.
59:2. **Destructive-command tripwire.** Shell-words tokenization in TypeScript (`cli/src/security.ts`) and Rust (`core/src/runner.rs`) stops obviously destructive commands (`rm -rf /`, `mkfs`, raw block device writes, fork bombs) without false positives on legitimate project commands (`rm -rf ./build`, `rm -rf /tmp/x`, `grep reboot`, `echo shutdown`, `chown -R me /srv`). *Limit:* this is explicitly a convenience tripwire to catch obvious mistakes, **not** a security boundary. Alternative invocations (`find / -delete`, `/bin/rm -rf /`, `rm -r -f /`, Python scripts) are documented non-goals that pass through by design. The sandbox (`--sandbox`) and approval posture (`review`) form the security boundary.
63:6. **Container sandbox and argv isolation.** `--sandbox` confines execution using Linux Bubblewrap (`bwrap`) or Docker. The sandbox argv is constructed as a direct array without shell wrapping (REQ-SEC-109), preventing shell escaping flaws on complex workspace paths. In `--read-only` mode, `$HOME` is mounted as `--tmpfs $HOME`, completely masking SSH keys and dotfiles from commands (REQ-SEC-104); without bwrap, strict path confinement rejects paths outside the workspace. *Limit:* full container sandboxing requires `bwrap` or Docker on the host.
64:7. **Process group lifecycle and residual setsid escape risk.** The runner registers child process groups at spawn and terminates entire groups (`killpg`) on turn cancel, client crash, or process shutdown (REQ-AGT-109, REQ-SEC-106). Background services explicitly registered survive turn cancel but are cleaned on client exit. *Limit:* commands that explicitly invoke `setsid()` or create a new session ID escape the process group boundary unless Bubblewrap (`--sandbox`) or Docker isolation is enabled (`bwrap` uses `--die-with-parent` and PID namespaces to guarantee all descendants are swept). Documented residual risk: in unsandboxed mode, processes that detach with `setsid()` will outlive cancel sweeps.

## 2. TypeScript Orchestration Layer (`cli/`)

- **`AutonomousAgent` (`agent.ts`)**: Manages the iterative decision loop, token budgeting, prompt construction, and tool execution.
- **`InteractiveRepl` (`repl.ts`)**: Readline REPL with tab autocompletion, multiline input, direct shell escapes, and slash commands. Used when no terminal is attached, or with `nexus repl`.
- **`SidecarServer` (`sidecar.ts`)**: Runs the agent for the Rust live TUI (`core/src/bin/nexus_tui`), speaking NDJSON over stdio. The TUI owns all keyboard input, including approval input safety.
- **`LocalLlmClient` (`client.ts`)**: Streaming SSE OpenAI-compatible client with automatic auth token discovery and token rotation retry.
- **`CheckpointManager` (`checkpoint.ts`)**: Creates safe git and tree checkpoints before every turn and manages workspace rollbacks (`/undo`).
- **`McpClientManager` (`mcp.ts`)**: Stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 client connecting external MCP servers from `~/.config/nexus/mcp.json`.
- **`SkillManager` (`skills.ts`)**: Auto-discovers and dynamically loads `SKILL.md` documents on-demand.
- **`PluginManager` (`plugins.ts`)**: Lifecycle hook manager supporting `onTurnStart`, `onToolCall`, `onToolResult`, and custom tool registration.
- **`TerminalUI` (`ui.ts`)**: Formatted terminal output with live spinners, colored diffs, milestone plans, and secret scrubber.

**Code health numbers**
- Largest TypeScript files: `agent.ts` 8202 lines, `client.ts` 2484, `repl.ts` 1971, `upgrade.ts` 1701, `tester.ts` 1653, `doctor.ts` 1501, `sidecar.ts` 1462, `checkpoint.ts` 1365.
- Largest Rust files: `live_state.rs` 5535, `live_view.rs` 5425, `live.rs` 1422, `file_ops.rs` 2123, `runner.rs` 1387.
- `AutonomousAgent` is a single class starting at `agent.ts:936`. I did not measure individual function lengths.
- Tests: 282 `*.test.*` files under `cli/`, about 3,367 `it(` or `test(` calls (rg estimate), and about 435 Rust test attributes. A cli suite run takes 12 to 20 minutes (`release.yml`).

**Gaps and strengths**
The clearest gaps are reach and measurement. Nexus ships Linux x86_64 only, with no macOS, Windows or arm64 build, no IDE or ACP integration, no GitHub Action, and no session fork. It also has no Gemini, Bedrock or Vertex provider, no `stream-json` output, and no published SWE-bench or Terminal-Bench result. Its only OS-level isolation is opt-in bubblewrap or Docker, and the default posture is approval prompts rather than containment. The code is concentrated in very large files: `agent.ts` at 8.2k lines, and about 5k lines each in two TUI state and view files. The strengths are in correctness and supply chain. These are verification-gated completion (verifier evidence, requirement ledger, type-check evidence, convergence stopping), pre-turn checkpoints with `/undo`, worktree merge gated on a receipt, reproducible attested release builds, a cautious blackbox eval runner, and context-window discovery across local servers. Documentation is unusually candid about limits, though the volume of assessment documents next to a README that still says v1.1.3 is stable makes onboarding heavier than the code needs.
